name: edge_vertex_map_rows
description: How the reference editor's statistics panel builds the edge domain's vertex-map rows, and what makes one edge count for one row. Read STATICALLY off the reference's own unstripped shipped libraries -- no engine boot, no display, no behavioural stand. The row this closes had carried a NAMED HYPOTHESIS for the enumerator ('the same edge-domain flag the weld-time edge-map copy tests'); the read REFUTES it, and the refutation is recorded here with its margin so nobody re-adopts it.
source: Static disassembly of the reference editor's shipped libraries (objdump/nm over the unstripped symbol tables). Zero boots.
read_from: Read at the reference's own compute sites: the per-domain statistics vtable's initialiser (which builds the row lists), the layer-wide map collector it calls, the per-element counting callback, and the map-type registry's start-up writer. Routine names, libraries and addresses live in the PRIVATE toolcard for this task -- they are the reference's own identifiers and deliberately do not cross into this tree. What is reproducible from here is the LAW.

domain_categories.law: The edge domain of the statistics panel has exactly four categories, in this fixed order. The vertex-map category is index 2. Edge selection sets are a SEPARATE category (index 3) fed by a different collector, so a selection set can never appear among the vertex-map rows.

row_enumeration.law: The vertex-map rows are collected by scanning the layers for every map whose KIND is a member of a fixed, hard-coded whitelist held per domain. It is a whitelist of kinds, NOT a predicate over a per-kind capability flag. The edge domain's whitelist has exactly one member: the subdivision crease-weight kind. The collection is deduplicated by (kind, name) and sorted, and it spans foreground AND background layers.
row_enumeration.header_row_means: every collected map, no kind or name filter

refuted_enumerator_candidate.candidate: the per-kind edge-domain capability flag used by the weld-time edge-map copy (registry row 39)
refuted_enumerator_candidate.why_it_is_not_degenerate: The flag and the whitelist are different SETS on the shipped registry, so the two candidates predict different row lists on any mesh that carries an edge selection set.
refuted_enumerator_candidate.observable_consequence: Under the refuted candidate every edge selection set would be listed twice -- once in the vertex-map rows and once in its own category.

edge_membership.law: An edge counts for a row iff the row's map holds an entry for the edge's UNORDERED vertex pair. The lookup tries the pair in the stored order and, on a miss, tries it reversed; the reversed try is inside the map accessor itself, so every caller of it -- the vertex-map count, the selection-set count and the weld-time copy alike -- gets unordered-pair semantics with no extra code.
edge_membership.reversal_lives_in: the map accessor, not the caller

ours.note: Our map-kind registry declares exactly ONE edge-domain kind, the crease-weight map, and our selection sets are not map kinds at all -- so our 'one row per edge-domain kind' rule and the reference's one-kind whitelist AGREE by construction. Our edges are keyed by a canonical undirected vertex pair, so the unordered-pair half is structural on our side.
